version_note: 0.2.1 from crates.io, built and run inside a rust:slim container on 2026-08-31.
derivation: Mapping derived from solsec's OWN rule descriptions in docs/SECURITY_CHECKS.md, fetched and read BEFORE any corpus run, not from which rules happened to fire.
right_of_reply: Not sent to the solsec author. Under PROTOCOL.md this mapping should be offered to them for correction before the result is treated as final, and their correction published.
unmapped_note: solsec's remaining 5 rules target memory-safety (unsafe transmute/pointer ops), reentrancy (CEI pattern), generic bounds checking, and arithmetic overflow. None of these name a class in this corpus by the rule's own description, so none are mapped even though 'unchecked_account' brushes up against account-data-matching in spirit; its description (unsafe transmute/raw pointer access) is a narrower and different bug than 1-account-data-matching's actual pattern (missing owner check before typed deserialisation via try_from_slice), so it was not mapped on a strict reading of the rule's own text.
structural_gaps: 8 of 11 classes have no solsec rule at all under this reading: 1-account-data-matching, 2-owner-checks, 3-type-cosplay, 4-initialization, 5-arbitrary-cpi, 6-duplicate-mutable-accounts, 8-pda-sharing, 9-closing-accounts, 10-sysvar-address-checking. solsec's 8 rules target a different, broader slice of Rust/Solana security hygiene (memory safety, reentrancy, generic input validation, arithmetic) than the 11 sealevel-attacks classes, and only 2 of the 11 classes have any corresponding rule.
